query: For eutectic high-entropy alloys intended for structural applications, what single intervention could simultaneously increase strength and ductility? Formulate one testable hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Applying cryo-rolling followed by an optimized annealing treatment to a cast eutectic high-entropy alloy (e.g., AlCoCrFeNi2.1) refines the lamellar microstructure into an ultrafine-grained duplex structure that simultaneously increases both the yield strength and ductility compared to a conventional cold-rolled and annealed microstructure.
generation.material_initial_state: A cast eutectic high-entropy alloy with a coarse lamellar (dual-phase) microstructure, typical of as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEAs.
generation.intervention: Cryogenic rolling (cryo-rolling) followed by a controlled annealing process.
generation.conditions: The treatment is conducted by cryo-rolling at cryogenic temperatures, then annealing at a temperature that is optimized to induce microstructure refinement without coarsening, under quasi-static tensile testing conditions at room temperature.
generation.structural_mediator: The process refines the eutectic lamellae into an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure, which increases the density of phase boundaries and grain boundaries.
generation.mechanism: The refined ultrafine-grained structure enhances both strength and ductility: increased strength is achieved by grain-boundary strengthening and hindering of dislocation motion, while the duplex microstructure allows for better strain partitioning between phases, leading to improved ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to a baseline cold-rolled and annealed microstructure, the cryo-rolled and annealed alloy is expected to exhibit a higher yield strength (potentially on the order of a 20-30% increase) and improved elongation (e.g., ductility improvement by a few percentage points), although the exact magnitude may depend on processing details and composition.
generation.baseline: EHEA processed via conventional cold-rolling followed by annealing.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis is expected to hold for eutectic high-entropy alloys with similar lamellar compositions and phase distributions under quasi-static mechanical loading at room temperature; deviations in alloy composition or processing parameters may limit the effect.
generation.uncertainty: The precise quantitative enhancement in strength and ductility is uncertain and may be influenced by specific cryo-rolling and annealing conditions as well as the exact eutectic composition.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples of the target eutectic high-entropy alloy. Process one set using conventional cold-rolling and annealing (baseline) and the other set using cryo-rolling followed by the same annealing treatment. Conduct standardized quasi-static tensile tests at room temperature.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the cryo-rolled and annealed samples do not show a statistically significant increase (e.g., at least ~20% higher yield strength and a measurable improvement in ductility) compared to the cold-rolled and annealed samples, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: To tackle the aforementioned problems, eutectic HEAs (EHEAs) [] were proposed. On the one hand, EHEAs should have the general character of traditional eutectic alloys. In this sense, EHEAs should have better fluidity and thus better castability and less casting defects [,]. On the other hand, EHEAs as one kind of in-situ composites with lamellar or rod-like eutectic microstructures might reach the balance between strength and ductility via mixing the soft FCC phase with the hard BCC phase or intermetallic compound [,,,,,,,,]. Some EHEAs indeed have outstanding properties. Lu et al. [] reported the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA with simultaneous high strength (944 MPa) and good ductility (25.6%). The excellent mechanical properties do not depend significantly on derivation of eutectic compositions []. After cold-rolling and annealing, its strength reached up to 1.2 GPa and its elongation could remain at about 12% []. After cryo-rolling and annealing, its strength could reach up to 1.47 GPa while its ductility could even increase to 14% []. He et al. [,] designed the CoCrFeNiNbx EHEAs and found that the microstructures were stable from 600 °C to 900 °C.

reading.lever: Apply cryo-rolling and annealing to refine the eutectic lamellar structure, yielding an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure.
reading.why: This intervention directly addresses both strength and ductility limitations by leveraging controlled deformation and phase refinement proven effective in related eutectic HEAs.
